hindi: कटु, अम्ल और लवण रस पित्त को; मधुर, अम्ल और लवण रस कफ को; तथा कटु, तिक्त और कषाय रस वात को कुपित करते हैं।
english: Pungent, sour and salty tastes aggravate Pitta; sweet, sour and salty aggravate Kapha; and pungent, bitter and astringent provoke Vāta (samīraṇa).

text_flags.why: svādu + amla gives svādvamla with long ā (as in unit 66 'svādvamlalavaṇā'); the Devanagari also lacks the ā sign (स्वद्वम्ल), a typing slip; metre is unaffected (syllable count 16 either way).

Brackets are unbalanced within the lines: ')' closes line a and '(' opens line b, so the pair seems misplaced; the bracket most likely encloses the whole verse ('(kaṭvamla... ||)'). Possible typing error in the bracket placement.

notes: The printed brackets around this verse probably mark it as an additional or doubtful verse in this edition (it stands between 66 and 67 and is numbered 66.1); its status was not checked against other editions. kopayanti governs all three subjects (pittaṃ, kapham, samīraṇam). samīraṇa is a synonym for vāyu, rendered Vāta per glossary. The verse is the counterpart of unit 66 (tastes that pacify each doṣa).
